name: Natural gas; combusted in industrial boiler
description: Provides an estimated national mix of industrial natural gas boiler combustion technologies in the US. Size shares follow an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022).

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Mix year 2017, based on the equipment inventory vintage used in an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022) and related national inventory data.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Based on US facility reported data.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: US average mix of industrial natural gas boilers. Capacity shares: 3 percent <10 million Btu per hour (uncontrolled), 31 percent from 10-100 million Btu per hour (low NOx burners), and 66 percent >100 million Btu per hour (low NOx burners), from an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022).
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Mix of NETL unit processes already in the US Life Cycle Inventory. Small boilers (less than 10 million Btu per hour) use the uncontrolled inventory; many units in that size class fall below NSPS Subpart Dc coverage for steam generating units. Mid-size and large boilers use low NOx burner inventories. Control technology is not reported in the size inventory used for mix shares, so this is a documented technology choice for an unspecified national average: EPA AP-42 Chapter 1.4 identifies low NOx burners and flue gas recirculation as the most common NOx controls on natural gas boilers, and NSPS Subparts Dc (10 to 100 million Btu per hour) and Db (greater than 100 million Btu per hour) make combustion controls the expected technology for those size classes. Selective catalytic and non-catalytic reduction and flue gas recirculation unit processes are excluded from this unspecified average.
processDocumentation.restrictionsDescription: All information can be accessed by everybody.
